chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr or someone else, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:

I said to him: 'May I be your sacrifice! The Shia are asking you about the interpretation of this verse: "About what are they asking one another? About the great news."' He said: 'That is up to me. If I desire, I shall inform them, and if I desire, I shall not inform them.'

Then he said: 'But I will inform you of its interpretation.' I said: '"About what are they asking one another?"' He said: 'It is about Amir al-Mu'minin, blessings of God upon him. Amir al-Mu'minin, blessings of God upon him, used to say: There is no sign of God, Mighty and Majestic, that is greater than me, and no news of God greater than me.'

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful — title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)
key_terms.الآية: Sign/verse — used here in its dual sense as both a Quranic verse and a divine sign, applied to the Imam
key_terms.النبأ العظيم: The Great News — interpreted here as referring to Imam Ali and the Imamate, not just a general eschatological event
key_terms.صلوات الله عليه: Blessings of God upon him — honorific used for the Imams in Shia tradition

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of 'the Great News' (al-Naba al-'Azim) in Quran 78:2?
ai.summary: In this narration, Abu Hamza al-Thumali asks Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) about the Shia community's question regarding the Quranic verse 'About what are they asking one another? About the great news' (78:1-2). The Imam reveals its esoteric interpretation: it refers to Imam Ali (Amir al-Mu'minin), who himself declared that no divine sign or tidings is greater than him. This reflects the Shia theological doctrine that the Imams are the greatest signs (ayat) of God on earth, embodying divine guidance and authority for humanity.
